reason: The spring-free drive jams outright at a modest friction rise; the lead does not. Measured here with the model unchanged (its own 'check' mode, fast Bench(60,160), the VERIFIED placement a_s 9.5 / psi 150, only mu changed): the stage-1 pin's cap-side pressure angle is 35.25 deg at the dwell exit (K 0), which K crosses on its way to every pose that needs it off rest (188 of the 371 taken bench poses, verify/desmo-slipper-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen_fix.json extra.th_margin.forced). Against the model's own gate 43 - atan(mu) it holds to mu 0.135 (dK_lim 44.5 from stage 2, fast plain 14.84) and fails from mu 0.14 (gate 35.03): dK_lim 0, K never leaves the dwell, fast plain 86.71 (reach 0.344, follow 0.65). The cliff sits at mu 0.136 (model rule) or 0.172 (the judge's 45 - atan(mu) rule). The claim and the verifier read the gate at mu 0.087 and 0.12 only (0.91 deg of margin at 0.12). The lead's stage 1 ROLLS (MR63ZZ on the lobe), so at mu 0.15 it keeps dK_lim 43.0 and fast 14.88 (docs/alignment/remeasure/slipper-nose-knuckle-3r_bench_r125_mu15.json). The design's complexity gain (15.75 vs 18.25) is bought partly by turning a rolling pair into a sliding pair parked under 1 deg from a friction-dependent jam gate: on a 440C pin in a DLC groove, mu 0.14 is a dry-running or worn-grease value, not an exotic one. The score cannot see it (it reads the drive at one mu). Not gamed: the score does not rank the design above the lead (18.95 vs 18.49), and no hard rule is broken. Action: carry a mu column (0.12 / 0.15) in every sliding-drive claim, and re-place stage 1 for cap-side PA margin at the dwell exit (or keep the stage-1 roller and delete only the spring); the CAD must state the groove's lubrication and coating.

reason: The model declares a groove gate it never enforces, and the verified number depends on that. The docstring and constant RC_MIN 1.5 say 'groove centreline radius >= 1.5 in link 2's frame ... The first failing step cuts the drive range dK_lim', but the cut list omits it (computed only into lim_by_gate). At the claim placement it fails at K 0.25 deg (rc_min 0.37 mm, below the 0.75-mm pin radius: the milled groove loses its inner wall, and the claim's 9-point corner scan missed the resulting 0.273-deg play at K 42 that the verifier's dense scan found). At the VERIFIED placement the centreline radius is still 0.99-1.0 mm over the whole onset corner (K 0.77-8.6) and 1.05 at K 46 (docs/concepts/verify/desmo-slipper-knuckle-3r_groove_scan_fix.json prof); the stage-1 record at mu 0.15 reads lim_by_gate.radius 0.5 deg. Enforced as written, the gate would stop K at about 0.5-0.8 deg, i.e. the drive could not leave the dwell. The verifier replaced the gate with a direct play measurement (dense scan 0.188 deg worst inside the taken K range, 0.241 at K 49.4), which is the right physics for slop, but not for the wear the 1.5 rule guards: with a 1.52-mm groove the inner wall at the onset corner is a ridge of radius 0.99 - 0.76 = 0.23 mm, loaded by the pin at every dwell exit. Its wear turns directly into K play, which the fold margin cannot afford (finding T3). The onset blend that softens this corner sits at its search-box edge (blend 10.0 of 0-10). Action: either enforce the declared gate (and report what the design scores) or retire it in the model's docstring with the measured reason; state the ridge radius and its contact stress on the L1 CAD.
